text: Which two tasks should be performed immediately after creating a new AWS account? (Choose two.)

options.A: Enable MFA on the root user
options.C: Create an IAM user with AdministratorAccess for daily work
options.D: Share the root credentials with the operations team

explanation_en: Best practice is to secure the root user with MFA and a strong password, then create an IAM administrative user for day-to-day work. The root user cannot be deleted and credentials must never be shared.
tip: Root hardening checklist: MFA on, strong password, delete root access keys, create an IAM admin, then stop using root. 'Delete the root user' is impossible and always a fake option.

text: Which task can ONLY be performed by the AWS account root user?
explanation_en: A small set of tasks are reserved for the root user, including closing the account, changing the account name or email, changing the support plan, and restoring IAM user permissions.
tip: Root-only tasks: close the account, change account name/email/root password, change support plan, restore IAM permissions, register as a seller, enable MFA delete on S3. Everything else can be delegated to IAM.

text: An application running on EC2 needs to read objects from an S3 bucket. What is the most secure way to grant this access?

options.A: Store an access key and secret in the application's configuration file
options.B: Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance
options.D: Embed the root user credentials in the code

explanation_en: IAM roles provide temporary, automatically rotated credentials to the instance so no long-term keys are stored anywhere.
tip: Whenever an AWS SERVICE needs to call another AWS service, the answer is an IAM ROLE. Any option that stores an access key on disk or in code is automatically wrong.

text: What is the principle of least privilege?

options.A: Grant every user administrator access and monitor their behavior
options.B: Grant only the permissions required to perform a task
options.C: Grant permissions to groups but never to roles
options.D: Grant permissions only through the root user

explanation_en: Least privilege means starting with minimal permissions and granting only what is required for the task.
tip: Least privilege = start with NOTHING and add only what is needed. Any answer that starts broad and narrows later, or that grants admin 'temporarily', violates it.

text: Which service provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports such as SOC and PCI?
explanation_en: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for downloading AWS audit reports and agreements.
tip: ARTIFACT = download compliance documents. CONFIG = track resource configuration changes. TRUSTED ADVISOR = best-practice checks. INSPECTOR = vulnerability scanning of workloads. Four different jobs, frequently mixed in options.

text: Which service continuously monitors AWS accounts for malicious or unauthorized behavior using threat intelligence?
explanation_en: GuardDuty is the intelligent threat detection service that analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs for suspicious activity.
tip: Security service map: GUARDDUTY = threat detection. INSPECTOR = vulnerability assessment. MACIE = finds sensitive data in S3. SHIELD = DDoS. WAF = web attacks (SQL injection, XSS). DETECTIVE = investigate findings.

text: Which service discovers and classifies sensitive data such as credit card numbers stored in Amazon S3?
explanation_en: Macie uses machine learning to find and classify sensitive data, including personally identifiable information, in S3 buckets.
tip: MACIE is the only service tied to S3 and SENSITIVE DATA / PII. If the stem mentions credit card numbers, PII or personal data sitting in S3, it is Macie.

text: Which two protections does AWS Shield Standard provide at no additional cost? (Choose two.)

options.A: Protection against common network and transport layer DDoS attacks
options.B: Automatic protection for all AWS customers
options.C: 24/7 access to the DDoS Response Team
options.D: Cost protection for scaling charges during an attack

explanation_en: Shield Standard is enabled automatically for every AWS customer at no cost and defends against common layer 3 and 4 DDoS attacks. The response team and cost protection are Shield Advanced features.
tip: SHIELD STANDARD = free, automatic, layers 3/4. SHIELD ADVANCED = paid, adds the DDoS Response Team, cost protection and layer 7 coverage. If the option mentions a support team or billing credits, it is Advanced.

text: An application must be protected from SQL injection and cross-site scripting attacks. Which service should be used?
explanation_en: AWS WAF inspects the content of application-layer requests and can block SQL injection and XSS patterns. Security groups and NACLs work at the network layer and cannot inspect request content.
tip: WAF is the only option that reads the CONTENT of a request (layer 7): SQL injection, XSS, bad user agents, geo blocking. Security groups and NACLs only see IPs, ports and protocols.

text: What is the difference between a security group and a network ACL? (Choose two.)

options.A: Security groups are stateful; NACLs are stateless
options.B: Security groups can deny traffic explicitly; NACLs cannot
options.C: Security groups apply to instances; NACLs apply to subnets
options.D: NACLs are evaluated only for outbound traffic

explanation_en: Security groups are stateful and attach to instances or network interfaces. NACLs are stateless, attach to subnets, and are the only one of the two that supports explicit deny rules.
tip: Four-word memory aid: SG = INSTANCE, STATEFUL, ALLOW-ONLY. NACL = SUBNET, STATELESS, ALLOW AND DENY. It is impossible to write a security group rule that denies.

text: Which service stores, rotates, and manages database credentials automatically?
explanation_en: Secrets Manager stores secrets such as database credentials and can rotate them automatically on a schedule.
tip: SECRETS MANAGER = stores secrets and ROTATES them automatically (paid). Parameter Store = stores config and secrets, free tier, no built-in rotation. KMS = manages encryption KEYS, not credentials. ACM = TLS certificates.

text: Which statement about AWS KMS is correct?

options.A: KMS keys are global and can be used in any region
options.B: KMS uses customer master keys to encrypt data
options.C: KMS can encrypt an existing unencrypted EBS volume in place
options.D: KMS replaces the need for IAM permissions

explanation_en: KMS manages customer master keys used to encrypt data. Keys are regional, existing EBS volumes cannot be encrypted in place, and access to KMS is still governed by IAM and key policies.
tip: Three KMS facts the exam repeats: keys are REGIONAL, the key is a CMK, and EBS encryption must be chosen AT CREATION - snapshot, copy encrypted, restore is the only path for an existing volume.

text: Which service issues and manages free public TLS/SSL certificates for use with AWS services?
explanation_en: AWS Certificate Manager provisions, manages, and renews TLS certificates for use with load balancers, CloudFront, and API Gateway at no cost for public certificates.
tip: ACM = certificates (free for public ones, auto-renewed). KMS = encryption keys. CLOUDHSM = a dedicated hardware module when regulations demand single-tenant key storage.

text: A regulated customer must have exclusive, single-tenant control of the hardware storing their encryption keys. Which service meets this requirement?
explanation_en: CloudHSM provides dedicated, single-tenant hardware security modules that the customer controls exclusively. KMS is a shared, multi-tenant managed service.
tip: The words DEDICATED HARDWARE, SINGLE-TENANT or FIPS 140-2 Level 3 point to CloudHSM. If the stem is happy with a managed shared service, it is KMS.

text: Which service records API calls made in an AWS account for auditing purposes?
explanation_en: CloudTrail logs API activity, capturing who did what, when, and from where. CloudWatch tracks performance, Config tracks configuration state, and X-Ray traces application requests.
tip: WHO DID WHAT = CloudTrail. HOW IS IT PERFORMING = CloudWatch. WHAT DOES THE CONFIGURATION LOOK LIKE NOW AND BEFORE = Config. WHERE IS MY REQUEST SLOW = X-Ray.

text: Which service evaluates whether your AWS resource configurations comply with defined rules over time?
explanation_en: AWS Config records resource configurations, keeps a history of changes, and evaluates them against compliance rules.
tip: The words COMPLIANT CONFIGURATION, CONFIGURATION HISTORY or DRIFT FROM A RULE point to AWS Config. If it is about a specific API call, it is CloudTrail instead.

text: Which two are valid ways to allow an employee to sign in to AWS using existing corporate credentials? (Choose two.)

options.C: AWS IAM Identity Center connected to Active Directory
options.D: Creating a separate IAM user with the same password

explanation_en: Federation through SAML 2.0 or IAM Identity Center integrated with a corporate directory allows single sign-on with existing credentials. Sharing root credentials or duplicating passwords are both insecure and are not federation.
tip: FEDERATION means an EXTERNAL identity provider authenticates the user and AWS trusts the result. Valid standards: SAML 2.0, Active Directory, OpenID Connect, Cognito for web/mobile.

text: Which statement about IAM policies is correct?

options.A: An explicit deny always overrides an allow
options.B: An explicit allow overrides an explicit deny
options.C: Policies are evaluated in the order they were attached
options.D: A user with no policies has full access by default

explanation_en: IAM evaluation is deny by default: access requires an explicit allow, and any explicit deny anywhere overrides all allows.
tip: Two rules cover every IAM evaluation question: implicit DENY unless something allows, and an EXPLICIT DENY always wins. Order of attachment never matters.

text: An organization wants to prevent any account in an organizational unit from using services outside approved regions. Which feature does this?

options.A: Service control policies in AWS Organizations
options.B: IAM user policies in each account

explanation_en: Service control policies set the maximum available permissions for accounts in an organization, acting as a guardrail no IAM policy in the account can exceed.
tip: An SCP is a CEILING, not a grant - it can never give permissions, only limit them. If the stem says 'across all accounts' or 'no one, including administrators, may', the answer is an SCP.

text: Which two methods can make an object in an S3 bucket publicly readable? (Choose two.)
explanation_en: Public or anonymous access to S3 is granted only through bucket policies and ACLs. IAM policies apply to identities in your account and can never grant anonymous access, and security groups do not apply to S3.
tip: ANONYMOUS access = bucket policies and ACLs only. IAM USER POLICIES CANNOT MAKE ANYTHING PUBLIC - that is one of the most reliable eliminations in the whole exam. Security groups never apply to S3.

text: Which two statements about encryption on AWS are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: Server-side encryption protects data at rest
options.C: Server-side encryption protects data in transit
options.D: Encryption at rest removes the need for access controls

explanation_en: Server-side encryption protects stored data, and TLS protects data moving over the network. Encryption never replaces IAM and resource-level access control.
tip: AT REST = SSE, KMS, EBS/S3 encryption. IN TRANSIT = TLS/HTTPS, VPN, client-side encryption before upload. Never let an option claim encryption removes the need for permissions.

text: An auditor asks for evidence that every IAM user has MFA enabled. What is the fastest way to produce this?

options.D: Review the AWS Artifact SOC report

explanation_en: The credential report is a CSV listing every IAM user with the state of their passwords, access keys, and MFA devices.
tip: CREDENTIAL REPORT = a CSV inventory of user credential hygiene (password age, key age, MFA on/off). It is a snapshot of STATE, never a log of activity.

text: Which service scans EC2 instances and container images for software vulnerabilities?
explanation_en: Amazon Inspector performs automated vulnerability assessments of EC2 instances, container images, and Lambda functions.
tip: INSPECTOR = vulnerabilities inside your workloads (unpatched CVEs, exposed network paths). GuardDuty = suspicious ACTIVITY. Macie = sensitive DATA. Different questions, similar-looking options.

text: Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for patching the guest operating system on an EC2 instance?

options.C: Shared equally between AWS and the customer

explanation_en: With EC2 the customer controls the guest operating system and is therefore responsible for patching it. For managed services such as RDS, AWS handles the underlying OS patching.
tip: EC2 = YOU patch the OS. RDS, Lambda, Fargate and other managed services = AWS patches it. The dividing line is whether you can log into the operating system.

text: Which two credentials are required for programmatic access to AWS? (Choose two.)
explanation_en: Programmatic access through the CLI or SDKs uses an access key ID and a secret access key. The username and password pair is only for console sign-in.
tip: Never mix the two credential pairs: PROGRAMMATIC = access key ID + secret access key. CONSOLE = username + password. This distinction is tested in almost every IAM question set.

text: Which compliance program applies to an application that stores US healthcare records?
explanation_en: HIPAA governs the handling of protected health information in the United States.
tip: Industry to standard: HEALTHCARE = HIPAA. CREDIT CARDS = PCI DSS. US GOVERNMENT = FedRAMP. FINANCIAL REPORTING = SOC/SOX. EU PERSONAL DATA = GDPR. Read the industry in the stem first.

text: What does enabling MFA Delete on an S3 bucket accomplish?

options.A: It requires MFA to permanently delete an object version or disable versioning
options.B: It encrypts every object with a customer master key
options.C: It prevents any object from ever being deleted
options.D: It requires MFA to read objects

explanation_en: MFA Delete adds a multifactor requirement before an object version can be permanently deleted or versioning can be suspended. It must be enabled by the root user.
tip: MFA Delete protects the DESTRUCTIVE actions only (permanent delete, suspend versioning), requires VERSIONING to be on, and can only be enabled by the ROOT user. It does not affect reads or encryption.

text: An IAM user is denied access to an S3 bucket even though their IAM policy allows it. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: An explicit deny in the bucket policy or a service control policy
options.B: The bucket is in a different availability zone
options.C: IAM policies do not apply to S3
options.D: The user has not enabled MFA

explanation_en: Access requires no explicit deny anywhere in the evaluation chain. A deny in the bucket policy, an SCP, or a permissions boundary overrides the IAM allow.
tip: When an ALLOW is not working, look for a DENY somewhere else: bucket policy, SCP, permissions boundary, or a session policy. Explicit deny always wins, no matter where it lives.

text: Which two statements about IAM groups are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: A group is a collection of IAM users
options.B: A group can be nested inside another group
options.C: Policies attached to a group apply to all its users
options.D: A group has its own access key ID and secret

explanation_en: Groups collect users and apply attached policies to all members. Groups cannot be nested and have no credentials of their own.
tip: Groups cannot be NESTED and have NO CREDENTIALS - those two facts kill most distractors. A group is purely a way to attach one policy to many users.

text: Which service centrally manages firewall rules across multiple accounts in an organization?
explanation_en: Firewall Manager applies WAF rules, Shield Advanced protections, and security group policies consistently across all accounts in an AWS Organization.
tip: The words CENTRALLY, ACROSS MULTIPLE ACCOUNTS or CONSISTENTLY point to Firewall Manager. WAF alone protects one distribution or load balancer at a time.

text: Which two are true about the AWS root user's access keys? (Choose two.)

options.A: They should be deleted as a security best practice
options.B: They are required for the CLI to function
options.C: They grant unrestricted access to the account
options.D: They cannot be created at all

explanation_en: Root access keys grant unrestricted access and AWS recommends deleting them. The CLI works fine with IAM user keys or roles, and root keys can technically be created, which is why the recommendation exists.
tip: Root access keys CAN exist but SHOULD NOT. If an option says they are required or impossible, it is wrong - the correct posture is 'delete them and use IAM instead'.

text: A company must prove to an external auditor that AWS datacenters meet ISO 27001. What should they provide?

options.A: The ISO certification downloaded from AWS Artifact

explanation_en: AWS Artifact provides the certifications and audit reports that attest to the compliance of AWS infrastructure.
tip: Evidence about AWS ITSELF comes from ARTIFACT. Evidence about YOUR OWN account comes from CloudTrail, Config and Trusted Advisor. Read whose compliance the auditor is asking about.

text: Which statement about temporary security credentials is correct?

options.A: They expire automatically after a defined period
options.B: They must be stored in the application source code
options.D: They can only be used by the root user

explanation_en: Temporary credentials issued by AWS STS, for example when assuming a role, are short-lived and expire automatically, which is what makes them safer than long-term keys.
tip: The whole security value of a ROLE is that its credentials EXPIRE and rotate automatically. Any option describing permanent credentials in code is describing the thing roles were invented to avoid.

text: Which two actions help protect against accidental data deletion in Amazon S3? (Choose two.)
explanation_en: Versioning preserves previous versions of an object, and MFA Delete adds a second factor before a version can be permanently removed.
tip: Data-protection pair for S3: VERSIONING (keeps old copies, off by default, set per bucket) plus MFA DELETE (blocks permanent deletion). Object Lock is the stronger WORM option if it appears.

text: Which two statements about AWS penetration testing policy are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: Customers may test their own resources for a set of approved services without prior approval
options.B: Customers may test any AWS service including other customers' resources
options.C: Denial of service testing requires prior authorization from AWS
options.D: Penetration testing is prohibited on AWS under all circumstances

explanation_en: AWS permits customers to perform security testing against their own resources for a list of approved services without prior approval, but stress and denial of service testing still requires authorization.
tip: You may test WHAT YOU OWN, on APPROVED SERVICES, WITHOUT asking. You may never test other customers, and DoS/stress testing always needs permission. The Acceptable Use Policy is the governing document.
